items.biophysicalMechanism: Rapid voltage-activated Na+ channel enriched on fast-spiking PV+ GABAergic interneuron axons; sustains high-frequency inhibitory firing.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Somatodendritic and proximal AIS voltage-gated Na+ channel supporting action potential backpropagation into pyramidal dendrites.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Low-threshold voltage-gated Na+ channel concentrated at the distal AIS and Nodes of Ranvier; primary initiator of action potentials and saltatory conduction.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Threshold-amplifying ramp Na+ channel expressed in DRG nociceptors and sympathetic ganglia.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Juxtaparanodal and axonal low-threshold K+ channel dampening hyperexcitability and regulating spike timing precision.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: High-threshold somatodendritic delayed-rectifier K+ channel mediating action potential repolarization during repetitive firing.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: High-voltage-activating, rapidly deactivating K+ channel enabling sub-millisecond spike widths and >200 Hz firing in PV+ interneurons.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Fast-inactivating somatodendritic K+ channel enabling continuous low-frequency Type I firing and attenuating backpropagating dendritic spikes.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Non-inactivating subthreshold K+ channel mediating spike-frequency adaptation; inhibited by muscarinic Gq/PIP2 depletion.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: High-voltage-activated somatodendritic Ca2+ channel coupling postsynaptic depolarization to CaMKII/CREB gene transcription and dendritic plateaus.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Active-zone high-voltage Ca2+ channel tightly coupled to SNARE/synaptotagmin complexes to trigger fast synchronous vesicle exocytosis.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Presynaptic Ca2+ channel mediating neurotransmitter release at central and primary nociceptive dorsal-horn synapses; inhibited by Gi/o GPCR beta-gamma subunits.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Transient low-voltage-activated Ca2+ channel de-inactivated by hyperpolarization, driving rebound burst firing in thalamocortical and TRN neurons.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Pacemaker channel activated by hyperpolarization and facilitated by cAMP; stabilizes resting potential, generates rhythmic bursting, and shapes dendritic resonance.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Two-Pore-Domain Background Leak Potassium Channel (K2P / TREK / TASK)
items.biophysicalMechanism: Voltage-independent background K+ channel establishing baseline membrane leak conductance g_L and negative resting membrane potential.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Tetrameric glutamate-gated cation channel mediating fast excitatory postsynaptic currents (rise ~0.4 ms, decay ~2 ms); dynamic PSD trafficking underlies LTP/LTD expression.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Heterotetrameric receptor requiring both glutamate binding and postsynaptic depolarization to expel extracellular Mg2+ block, gating Ca2+ influx for LTP/STDP.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Ionotropic glutamate receptor expressed postsynaptically at hippocampal mossy-fiber CA3 synapses and presynaptically to modulate transmitter release.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Pentameric Cys-loop ligand-gated Cl- channel mediating fast phasic (synaptic) and tonic (extrasynaptic) hyperpolarizing and shunting inhibition.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Pentameric ACh-gated cation channel mediating fast neuromuscular transmission and presynaptic/interneuronal attentional gain in cortex.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Only ionotropic monoamine receptor; mediates fast serotonergic excitation of superficial cortical VIP+/5-HT3aR+ interneurons and vagal afferents.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Pentameric Cl- channel mediating fast postsynaptic reciprocal and Renshaw inhibition in spinal cord and brainstem motor circuits.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Trimeric ATP-gated cation channel expressed on microglia and astrocytes sensing activity-dependent or injury-induced purinergic signals.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Group I Metabotropic Glutamate Receptors (mGluR1 / mGluR5)
items.biophysicalMechanism: Perisynaptic Gq-coupled glutamate receptors triggering intracellular ER Ca2+ release, endocannabinoid synthesis, and mGluR-dependent LTD.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Group II/III Presynaptic Metabotropic Glutamate Receptors (mGluR2/3)
items.biophysicalMechanism: Presynaptic autoreceptors suppressing excess glutamate release Probability during high-frequency stimulation.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: GABA -> Gi/o -> Open GIRK K+ / Inhibit CaV
items.biophysicalMechanism: Obligate heterodimeric GPCR mediating slow (100–300 ms) postsynaptic K+ hyperpolarization and presynaptic release inhibition.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Activates PKA and DARPP-32 signaling in direct-pathway striatal dMSNs and prefrontal pyramidal cells to enhance excitability and LTP.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: Dopamine -> Gi/o -> Decrease cAMP / Open GIRK
items.biophysicalMechanism: Suppresses indirect-pathway striatal iMSN excitability and acts as a somatodendritic/presynaptic dopamine autoreceptor.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Mediate locus coeruleus neuromodulation: Alpha-2A closes HCN channels in dlPFC spines to strengthen working memory; Beta-1 facilitates hippocampal LTP.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Muscarinic Acetylcholine Receptors (M1 Gq / M2 Gi)
items.biophysicalMechanism: M1 activation suppresses Kv7 M-current to boost cortical pyramidal excitability and learning; M2 mediates vagal cardiac slowing and presynaptic inhibition.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: 5-HT1A hyperpolarizes raphe and hippocampal somata via GIRK channels; 5-HT2A excites Layer 5 cortical apical dendrites.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Abundant CNS presynaptic GPCR mediating retrograde depolarization-induced suppression of inhibition/excitation (DSI/DSE) and endocannabinoid LTD.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Mu-Opioid (MOR Gi) & Orexin (OX1/OX2 Gq) Peptide GPCRs
items.biophysicalMechanism: MOR inhibits nociceptive neurotransmitter release and disinhibits PAG analgesia; OX1/OX2 excite monoaminergic arousal nuclei to stabilize wakefulness.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Principal fast excitatory amino acid neurotransmitter across >80% of cortical and hippocampal synapses; synthesized from glutamine via phosphate-activated glutaminase.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Principal inhibitory neurotransmitter of the adult mammalian brain, synthesized from glutamate by GAD65 and GAD67.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Catecholamine synthesized from L-tyrosine via tyrosine hydroxylase and AADC; signals reward prediction errors, motivational vigor, and prefrontal gain.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Indolamine synthesized from L-tryptophan via TPH2 in brainstem raphe nuclei; regulates sleep-wake states, affective processing, and sensory modulation.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Synthesized from choline and acetyl-CoA by ChAT; mediates neuromuscular transmission, autonomic pre/parasympathetic signaling, and cortical attentional arousal.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: Binds Alpha-1, Alpha-2, and Beta-1..3 Adrenergic GPCRs
items.biophysicalMechanism: Synthesized from dopamine by dopamine beta-hydroxylase in locus coeruleus and sympathetic neurons; controls vigilance, network gain, and sympathetic tone.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: Binds H1, H2, H3, H4 GPCRs
items.biophysicalMechanism: Synthesized from L-histidine by histidine decarboxylase exclusively in hypothalamic tuberomammillary nucleus neurons; promotes cortical wakefulness.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: Binds GlyR / NMDA Co-agonist site & P2X/P2Y
items.biophysicalMechanism: Glycine serves both as the primary spinal inhibitory neurotransmitter and an obligatory co-agonist at NMDA receptors; ATP mediates fast purinergic gliotransmission.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Lateral hypothalamic neuropeptides stabilizing the wakefulness flip-flop switch; loss of orexin neurons causes narcolepsy instability.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: Binds Mu, Delta, and Kappa Opioid GPCRs
items.biophysicalMechanism: Peptide neuromodulators suppressing nociceptive transmission in the spinal dorsal horn and gating striatal direct/indirect pathways.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Co-released with glutamate from peptidergic C-fiber nociceptors in Dorsal Horn Lamina I to drive slow sustained depolarization and neurogenic inflammation.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Nonapeptides synthesized in hypothalamic PVN and supraoptic nuclei acting both as central social/autonomic neuromodulators and posterior pituitary hormones.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: GABAergic interneuron co-transmitters: NPY dampens epileptic hyperexcitability and stimulates arcuate feeding; VIP mediates cortical disinhibition and vasodilation.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Activity-dependent neurotrophin secreted during high-frequency stimulation; activates Ras-MAPK, PI3K-Akt, and PLCgamma to consolidate Late-LTP and spine growth.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Electrogenic Na+/K+-ATPase Pump (Alpha-3 Neuronal / Alpha-2 Glial)
items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: 3 Na+ Out / 2 K+ In per 1 ATP hydrolyzed
items.biophysicalMechanism: Consumes ~50% of brain ATP to maintain transmembrane Na+ and K+ concentration gradients required for Nernst potentials and secondary active transport.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Rapidly restores intracellular free [Ca2+] back to ~100 nM basal levels following action potentials and NMDA/CaV influx.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: KCC2 extrudes K+/Cl-; NKCC1 imports Na+/K+/2Cl-
items.biophysicalMechanism: Developmental upregulation of KCC2 lowers intracellular [Cl-], shifting E_GABA from depolarizing in immature neurons to hyperpolarizing (-75 mV) in mature CNS.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Excitatory Amino Acid Transporters EAAT1 (GLAST) & EAAT2 (GLT-1)
items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: Co-transports 3 Na+, 1 H+ in + 1 K+ out per Glutamate
items.biophysicalMechanism: Astrocytic perisynaptic glutamate uptake transporters clearing >90% of cleft glutamate within milliseconds to preserve point-to-point specificity and prevent excitotoxicity.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Neuronal (GAT-1) and astrocytic (GAT-3) transporters terminating synaptic GABA signaling and regulating tonic extrasynaptic inhibition.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: High-affinity presynaptic transporters clearing released monoamines from the extracellular space to control volume transmission duration.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Vesicular Neurotransmitter Transporters (VGLUT1/2, VGAT, VMAT2, VAChT)
items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: H+ Electrochemical Gradient Driven Vesicle Loading
items.biophysicalMechanism: Driven by vesicular V-ATPase proton pumps to concentrate neurotransmitters inside 40 nm synaptic vesicles up to 100 mM.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Core SNARE Fusion Complex (Synaptobrevin/VAMP2, Syntaxin-1, SNAP-25)
items.biophysicalMechanism: Zippers from N- to C-terminus to overcome hydration repulsion and fuse docked synaptic vesicles with the presynaptic active-zone plasma membrane.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: Binds 4–5 Ca2+ ions via C2A and C2B domains
items.biophysicalMechanism: Transmembrane vesicle protein that triggers sub-millisecond SNARE-mediated pore opening upon local CaV2 microdomain Ca2+ influx.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Catalytically near-diffusion-limited enzyme anchored in the synaptic cleft that terminates nicotinic and muscarinic ACh signaling in <1 ms.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: Binds up to 4 Ca2+ ions via EF-hand motifs
items.biophysicalMechanism: Ubiquitous Ca2+-binding transducer that conformationally activates CaMKII, calcineurin, adenylyl cyclase 1/8, and CaV channel CDI feedback.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Dodecameric holoenzyme comprising ~1–2% of total PSD protein; high-frequency Ca2+ influx triggers autonomous Thr286 phosphorylation, trapping GluA1 AMPARs at PSD-95 for LTP.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Activated by prolonged modest Ca2+ elevations during low-frequency stimulation; dephosphorylates Inhibitor-1 to activate PP1 and drive AMPAR endocytosis in LTD.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Adenylyl Cyclase – cAMP – Protein Kinase A (PKA) Cascade
items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: ATP -> cAMP -> PKA Catalytic Subunit Release
items.biophysicalMechanism: Activated by Gs-coupled GPCRs (D1, Beta-1) and inhibited by Gi/o (D2, Alpha-2, mGluR2); phosphorylates GluA1 Ser845, ion channels, and DARPP-32.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Phospholipase C-Beta (PLCbeta) – IP3 / DAG – PKC Cascade
items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: PIP2 -> IP3 (ER Ca2+ release) + DAG (PKC activation)
items.biophysicalMechanism: Activated by Gq-coupled receptors (mGluR1/5, M1, 5-HT2A, Alpha-1); mobilizes intracellular ER calcium waves and modulates TRP/K+ channels.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: cAMP Response Element-Binding Protein (CREB1) & IEGs (c-Fos, Arc)
items.biophysicalMechanism: Nuclear transcription factor phosphorylated by PKA, CaMKIV, and MAPK/ERK to induce immediate-early genes (Arc, c-Fos, BDNF) required for Late-LTP and memory consolidation.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.canonicalName: Postsynaptic Density Protein 95 (PSD-95 / DLG4) MAGUK Scaffold
items.ionOrLigandSpecificity: PDZ-domain scaffolding of NMDARs and TARP/AMPARs
items.biophysicalMechanism: Master structural organizer of the excitatory postsynaptic density aligning postsynaptic receptors opposite presynaptic active-zone nanocolumns.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.

items.biophysicalMechanism: Core molecular clockwork inside SCN neurons regulating circadian firing-rate rhythms via daily transcription and feedback repression of Per and Cry genes.
items.educationalScopeNote: Mechanistic biophysical and neurochemical specification only; non-clinical and non-pharmacological.
